title: Coming to America
tagline: A prince walks into a burger joint in Queens.
about: An African prince goes to Queens to find a bride and takes a job at a fast food joint.
cue: Serve the burgers when the Big Mick comes out at McDowell's.

    StartersGolden friesThin-cut fries, twice fried and salted straight from the oil.The golden side of McDowell’s.How to make itPrep 7 min, cook 20 min, 30 min waiting1kg russet potatoes2 L vegetable oil for frying1 tsp fine saltCut the potatoes into thin chips and soak in cold water, 30 min.Dry well.Heat the oil to 140°C and fry the potatoes, then rest, 12 min.Fry again at 190°C until golden and crisp, 8 min.Salt straight away and serve hot.My-T-Sharp boxing ringsThick-cut onion rings in a crisp beer batter, stacked high with a side of house sauce.As argued over at the barbershop next door. Joe Louis or Marciano?How to make itPrep 14 min, cook 29 min3 large brown onions200g plain flour1 tsp baking powder1 tsp salt250ml cold lager2 L vegetable oil, for frying125g mayonnaise2 tbsp sweet pickle relish1 tsp American mustard1/2 tsp paprika1 tsp white vinegarHeat the oil to 180°C in a deep pot, 10 min.Slice the onions 1.5cm thick, separate the rings and toss them in 50g of the flour.Whisk the rest of the flour, the baking powder and salt with the cold lager until smooth, 4 min.Dip the rings in the batter and fry in batches until golden and crisp, 3 minutes a batch. Drain and salt.Stir the mayonnaise, relish, mustard, paprika and vinegar into the house sauce.Stack the rings high and serve with the sauce.MainsBig MickDouble beef, cheese, pickles, shredded lettuce, onion and house sauce on a plain seedless three-piece bun.My buns have no seeds.How to make itPrep 27 min, cook 13 min100g mayonnaise2 tbsp sweet relish1 tsp yellow mustard1/2 tsp paprika1 tsp vinegar800g beef mince8 slices of American cheese6 plain seedless three-piece burger buns1/2 iceberg lettuce, shredded1 brown onion, diced12 dill pickle slicesMix the mayonnaise, relish, mustard, paprika and vinegar for the sauce.Shape the mince into 8 thin patties.Smash the patties in a hot pan and add the cheese.Toast the buns, 3 min.Build each with sauce, lettuce, onion, pickles and patties in the three-piece bun.Soul Glo fried chickenButtermilk-brined chicken, double dredged, fried and brushed with honey butter till it shines.Glistens like a Soul Glo ad. Napkins on the counter.How to make itAs written, serves 4Chicken brined in buttermilk and hot sauce, double-dredged, fried at 165°C, then brushed with hot honey butter so it shines.SweetsApple pyeCrisp baked pastry pocket filled with hot cinnamon apple and a pinch of brown sugar.This one is our version.How to make itPrep 5 min, cook 44 min, 15 min waiting3 Granny Smith apples, diced30g butter40g brown sugar1 tsp ground cinnamon1 tbsp lemon juice1 tsp cornflour2 sheets of frozen shortcrust pastry1 egg, beaten1 tbsp raw sugarCook the apples with the butter, brown sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice until just soft, 8 min.Stir in the cornflour mixed with a splash of water and cook until thick.Cool the filling, 15 min.Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut each pastry sheet into 4 rectangles, fill one half, fold over, crimp with a fork and cut two slits on top, 12 min.Brush with the egg, sprinkle with raw sugar and bake until crisp and golden, 22 min.Rose petal sugar crispsThin rosewater cookies, crushed dried rose petals pressed on top.Straight from Zamunda.How to make itPrep 25 min, cook 9 min125g butter, softened100g caster sugar1 tsp rose water200g plain flour1 tbsp dried rose petals, crushedBeat the butter with the sugar and rose water, then mix in the flour.Roll thin and cut into rounds.Press crushed rose petals on top.Bake at 170°C until just crisp at the edges, 9 min.Cool on the tray, 5 min.DrinksVanilla thick shakeVanilla ice cream and cold full-cream milk, blended thick.How about a Mick-Shake?How to make itPrep 10 min1.5 L vanilla ice cream600ml cold full cream milkChill four tall glasses, 5 min.Blend three scoops of ice cream with some of the milk until thick and smooth, one shake at a time.Pour into a chilled glass and serve with a wide straw.
